tr.td: Coronary angiography and percutaneous coronary intervention: occluded proximal left anterior descending artery treated with one drug-eluting stent; no other significant stenosis. Performed at an out-of-state hospital after a late presentation with continuing chest pain
Transthoracic echocardiography in the hospital: ejection fraction 45 percent with anterior and apical hypokinesis, no thrombus
Outpatient cardiac rehabilitation, phase 2: 36 sessions completed; exit exercise test 9 METs without angina, ischemic ECG changes, or arrhythmia
12-lead electrocardiogram: sinus rhythm 62/min, Q waves in V1 to V3 from the old anterior infarction, no acute ST change
Transthoracic echocardiography: ejection fraction 52 percent, mild apical hypokinesis, no thrombus or aneurysm, normal valves

High-intensity atorvastatin with ezetimibe added for LDL cholesterol above 55 mg/dL; recheck lipids 4 to 12 weeks after the change, then every 3 to 12 months
Metoprolol succinate and lisinopril for blood pressure below 130/80; basic metabolic panel 1 to 2 weeks after an ACE inhibitor change, then every 6 months; reassess the beta-blocker at one year
Cardiology consultation to establish local cardiology care, reassess left ventricular function, and advise on return to full-time work and on the duration of antiplatelet and beta-blocker therapy

Yearly influenza vaccine, pneumococcal vaccine, RSV vaccine, and current COVID-19 vaccine
